basis: Proposal A for the generator check of the G4 pilot (python -m egw_experiments generator-check), put forward on 2026-10-07. NOT adopted: with this file no report certifies (status 'proposed'; exit 3, every per-tolerance result labelled non-certifying). Approval is the student's act: a decision record, then a copy of this profile with status 'approved' and an approval naming who approved it, that decision record and the date. It is presented before the execution authorisation.

Profile A has three limits: zero relative overruns, a maximum relative lateness of 20 ms and an absolute first-to-last span deviation of 20 ms. Overruns and lateness are relative to the origin the check infers (the simulator does not record its schedule origin), so a constant offset common to every event is unobservable; the span deviation compares the first-to-last publish span, a difference of two publish stamps, with the scheduled span in absolute value and needs no origin. It applies the same three limits to the four pilot conditions: nominal at 11.2 msg/s (the 120 s and the 600 s runs), the load sweep at 10 and at 50 msg/s, and the soak at 11.2 msg/s.

max_overrun_events = 0. An overrun is an event published, relative to the inferred origin, at or after the due time of the next scheduled instant, the state in which the run loop skips its sleep and catches up (egw_simulator/runner.py, pace_until). Zero means that, relative to the inferred origin and within the check's resolution, no published event fell a full scheduled interval behind: no catch-up is detected. It does not mean zero late publish calls (each may be up to 20 ms late, relative) and says nothing about delivery.

max_relative_lateness_ms = 20.0. (i) It is below the smallest gap between scheduled instants of every pilot condition (22.4 ms at 50 msg/s, 100 ms at 11.2 msg/s, 112 ms at 10 msg/s), so it implies zero relative overruns at every pilot rate. (ii) It is 2.05 times the worst relative lateness the check measures on the three sealed nominal-scenario runs of the G3 battery, at 11.2 msg/s on this host: 9.762 ms (nominal-r02), 5.407 ms (controller_restart-r03) and 7.958 ms (controller_restart-r04), 20,160 events with no relative overrun and every 1 s window as scheduled (docs/evidence/g3-battery-2026-10). That baseline is an engineering basis only and is non-citable. It bounds the relative lateness of each event, not each inter-publish interval as such: two consecutive publish calls may be up to 20 ms closer together or further apart than scheduled (at 50 msg/s, between 2.4 ms and 42.4 ms apart instead of 22.4 ms).

max_span_deviation_ms = 20.0. The absolute deviation of the first-to-last publish span from the scheduled span, so the run is neither stretched nor shortened by more than 20 ms over its whole length. On the same three runs the deviation is at most 0.143 ms.

Costs. At 50 msg/s the scheduled gap (22.4 ms) is only 2.3 times the worst lateness seen at 11.2 msg/s, and no recorded run above 11.2 msg/s exists on this host. The soak has 40,320 events, so one host hiccup above 20 ms is not unlikely. A false NOT_SUSTAINED labels the run a pilot finding; the check changes no validity rule and no run's validity. A false SUSTAINED would mislead the pilot's feasibility finding. A NOT_SUSTAINED outcome is a pilot finding: not a licence to repeat the run, and not by itself an instrumentation failure.

Not proposed: alternative B (1000 ms lateness, 1000 ms span, overruns unbounded), set at the resolution of the 1 Hz samplers. It certifies a 0.9 s stall followed by catch-up, the failure the check exists to detect. A per-rate variant of A (the lateness limit equal to one scheduled interval: 100, 112 and 22.4 ms) is the other option left open.

What SUSTAINED under A would state: relative to the inferred origin and within the check's resolution, the client's publish calls kept the schedule over the whole run: no event a full scheduled interval late (no catch-up detected), none more than 20 ms late, and the first-to-last span within 20 ms of the scheduled span. It would not state zero late publish calls or deliveries, that every inter-publish interval was close to its schedule (two consecutive calls may be up to 20 ms closer together or further apart than scheduled), what the broker received (paho queues QoS 1 messages locally beyond 20 in flight), nor an absolute lateness (a constant offset c >= 0 common to every event is unobservable).
